newsitem.title: UK: British Gas says gas superhighway threatened.
newsitem.headline: British Gas says gas superhighway threatened.

text.p: British Gas Plc said on Thursday that its plans to construct a gas "superhighway" along the east coast of Britain might be shelved if a project to pipe gas from the North Sea to Norfolk wins government backing.
A spokesman for TransCo, British Gas's transportation arm, told Reuters that the company is supporting a rival scheme to transport gas to Teesside in the north-east of England.
He said the Teesside link would help feed a planned high pressure gas pipeline between East Anglia and Scotland, which would "create a superhighway from Scotland to Russia."
Without this scheme he said that building the extra link, at an estimated cost of 300 million stg, would be "uneconomic."
The dispute over the destination of the pipeline has pitted British Gas and Imperial Chemical Industries Plc against France's Elf Aquitaine, which is behind the Norfolk project.

Under Elf's proposals, which are backed by British Petroleum Plc and Shell Transport & Trading Co Plc, gas would be transported to the Continent via a proposed interconnector with Zeebrugge in Belgium. It would also be shipped to Scotland to supply BP's petrochemicals operations at Grangemouth.

TransCo claimed that the Teeside project would lead to lower gas prices in Britain and added that the superhighway link would sharply cut the costs of transporting gas from Scotland to the rest of Britain and Europe.
Development bodies on Teeside say the project could bring $1 billion of investment to the area and create around 500 jobs.
The final decision will be made by Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang. A DTI spokesman declined to comment on when a decision would be announced, adding "it is still being considered."
